title: Cap. X Arg. X: Augustine De praedest. sanct. 5 — common gifts do not discern; the grace that discerns good from evil is not common; God discerns you from another
pass_a_gloss: But let us hear Augustine cleaving to Paul’s footsteps and doctrine: De praedest. sanct. cap. 5. Are men, he says, discerned from men by these gifts which are common unto all men? A little after, The grace which discerns the good from the evil is not common both unto the good and unto the evil. Yet more plainly; God discerns thee from another, unto whom he has not given what he has given unto thee.
pass_b_english: Hear Augustine keeping Paul’s steps and teaching (De praedestinatione sanctorum 5): Are men set apart from men by gifts common to all? A little later: The grace that sets the good apart from the evil is not common to both. Still plainer: God sets you apart from another, to whom he has not given what he gave you.
source_text: Sed audiamus Augustinum Pauli vestigiis et doctrinae inhaerentem: De praedest. sanct. cap. 5. Numquid, inquit, per haec dona, quae omnibus communia sunt hominibus, discernuntur homines ab hominibus? Paulo post, Gratia quae bonos discernit a malis, non communis est et bonis et malis. Adhuc planius; Deus te discernit ab alio, cui non donavit, quod donavit tibi.
